column1: 24:1|Jesus was leaving the temple when his disciples came over to show him its buildings.|Connects the participial departure to the disciples’ approach in one natural sentence.

24:2|He replied, “Do you see all this? I tell you the truth: not one stone here will remain on another. Every one will be torn down.”|Retains the emphatic total destruction without stacking English negatives.

24:3|As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will this happen? What will be the sign of your coming and the end of the age?”|Separates the approach from two questions while retaining coming and age language.
24:4|Jesus answered, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.|Makes the warning idiomatic without narrowing deception to one group.
24:5|Many will come in my name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.|Retains the repeated many and the messianic claim.

24:6|You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. Do not be alarmed. These things must happen, but the end has not yet come.|Makes the warning audible in short sentences and retains the not-yet qualification.
24:7|Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places.|Preserves parallel conflicts while separating the list of disasters.
24:8|All this is the beginning of birth pains.|Retains the childbirth metaphor without interpreting its timetable.

24:9|“Then they will hand you over to suffering and kill you. All nations will hate you because of my name.|Replaces the unnatural hand-over-to-distress phrase while preserving persecution and motive.
24:10|At that time many will fall away, hand one another over, and hate one another.|Preserves the three linked actions and reciprocal betrayal.
24:11|Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.|Retains clear wording and the repeated many.
24:12|As lawlessness increases, the love of many will grow cold.|Expresses the causal development while retaining the cold-love image.
24:13|But whoever endures to the end will be saved.|Retains endurance and salvation without specifying an unstated mechanism.

24:14|This good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the inhabited world as a testimony to all nations. Then the end will come.|Preserves world and nations as distinct expressions and separates the final consequence.

24:15|“So when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of through the prophet Daniel standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—|Retains the scriptural expression and narrator’s reader-directed aside.
24:16|those in Judea must flee to the mountains.|Connects the command naturally to the preceding when-clause.
24:17|Anyone on the roof must not go down to collect things from the house.|Keeps the rooftop setting and urgent prohibition in ordinary English.
24:18|Anyone in the field must not turn back for a cloak.|Retains the specific garment and urgency without extra explanation.
24:19|How terrible those days will be for pregnant women and nursing mothers!|Expresses the lament as compassion for the specified women.
24:20|Pray that you will not have to flee in winter or on a Sabbath.|Makes flight verbal while preserving Matthew’s Sabbath detail.
24:21|For then there will be great suffering, unlike anything since the world began, and never to be repeated.|Preserves the unmatched distress and both temporal limits.

24:22|If those days were not cut short, no one would survive. But for the sake of the chosen, those days will be cut short.|Renders no-flesh-saved naturally in the threat to survival; retains chosen language.
24:23|“If anyone then tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There he is!’ do not believe it.|Preserves both competing location claims and the prohibition.

24:24|False christs and false prophets will arise and perform great signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.|Keeps the if-possible qualification without resolving its implications.
24:25|Remember, I have warned you beforehand.|Renders the attention marker as a reminder of the advance warning.

24:26|So if they tell you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out. If they say, ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.|Separates the two conditional warnings for listening clarity.
24:27|For as lightning flashes from east to west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.|Preserves the visible lightning comparison and established title.
24:28|Wherever the corpse is, the vultures will gather.|Retains the unexplained proverb and corpse rather than interpreting it.

24:29|“Immediately after the suffering of those days,
‘the sun will be darkened,
and the moon will give no light;
the stars will fall from heaven,
and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’|Lineates the scriptural cosmic imagery without turning it into a modern explanation.

24:30|Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.|Retains the ambiguous sign phrase, tribal mourning, and cloud imagery.

24:31|He will send his angels with a mighty trumpet, and they will gather his chosen from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.|Keeps angels, trumpet, and four winds rather than replacing them with explanations.

24:32|“Learn this lesson from the fig tree: when its branches grow tender and put out leaves, you know summer is near.|Makes the lesson introduction idiomatic while retaining the seasonal observation.
24:33|In the same way, when you see all these things, know that it is near, right at the door.|Keeps it/he ambiguity in a note rather than specifying an event in the text.
24:34|I tell you the truth: this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.|Retains this generation without changing it to a future generation or people.
24:35|Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.|Carries the emphatic negation through never while retaining the parallel.
24:36|“But no one knows that day or hour—not the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.|Preserves nor the Son in the pinned Greek without theological adjustment.
24:37|As it was in the days of Noah, so it will be at the coming of the Son of Man.|Clarifies the comparison’s English syntax while retaining the title.

24:38|In the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.|Retains both marriage actions and ordinary activities without moralizing them.

24:39|They knew nothing until the flood came and swept them all away. So it will be at the coming of the Son of Man.|Preserves ignorance and sudden removal without assigning roles to later taken/left sayings.
24:40|Then two people will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left.|Supplies people for natural English without specifying their fate.
24:41|Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and the other left.|Retains the explicitly female workers and parallel taken/left wording.
24:42|So stay awake, because you do not know what day your Lord will come.|Keeps the watchfulness image and day language.

24:43|Understand this: if the homeowner had known what time of night the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have let his house be broken into.|Renders night-watch timing naturally; preserves the hypothetical householder.
24:44|You too must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.|Retains unexpected timing without supplying a date or sequence.

24:45|“Who, then, is the faithful and wise servant whom the master has put in charge of his household to give them food at the proper time?|Makes the household responsibility explicit while preserving servant status in vocabulary.
24:46|Blessed is that servant if his master finds him doing this when he returns.|Clarifies the antecedent of doing so and the master’s return.
24:47|I tell you the truth: he will put that servant in charge of everything he owns.|Makes the promised responsibility idiomatic.
24:48|But suppose that wicked servant says to himself, ‘My master is taking a long time,’|Renders speech in the heart as internal speech and delay idiomatically.
24:49|and begins beating his fellow servants and eating and drinking with drunkards.|Preserves abuse of fellow servants and the second pattern of conduct.
24:50|That servant’s master will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know.|Removes a nested possessive while retaining both time expressions.
24:51|He will cut him in two and give him a place with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.|Retains the violent judgment and recurring final image without softening it.

25:1|“Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.|Retains the wedding setting and kingdom comparison; virgins identified in vocabulary.
25:2|Five were foolish and five were wise.|Retains the balanced division in a concise sentence.
25:3|The foolish ones brought their lamps but no oil with them.|Makes the contrast compact without inserting extra oil into the main text.
25:4|The wise ones brought jars of oil along with their lamps.|Renders containers concretely while preserving the additional supply.
25:5|The bridegroom was delayed, and they all grew drowsy and fell asleep.|Retains all ten sleeping; does not turn foolishness into sleep alone.
25:6|At midnight a shout rang out: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’|Makes the sudden midnight cry natural without adding the absent comes verb.
25:7|Then all the bridesmaids got up and put their lamps in order.|Renders preparation broadly rather than specifying wick-trimming as certain.
25:8|The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’|Keeps the request and immediate reason together.

25:9|But the wise ones answered, ‘There may not be enough for all of us. Go to the sellers and buy some for yourselves.’|Preserves the concern about sufficiency and direct instruction without adding a moral verdict.

25:10|While they were away buying oil, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.|Clarifies the simultaneous action and retains the shut door.
25:11|Later the other bridesmaids came too. ‘Lord, lord,’ they said, ‘open the door for us!’|Gives the repeated address audible dialogue without changing it to the narrator’s endorsement.
25:12|But he replied, ‘I tell you the truth: I do not know you.’|Preserves the denial of recognition and solemn introductory formula.
25:13|“So stay awake, because you know neither the day nor the hour.|Marks the return from parable dialogue to Jesus’ warning without adding a source-absent clause.
25:14|“It is also like a man about to travel. He called his servants and entrusted his property to them.|Divides the journey setup from the entrusted responsibility without redefining the comparison.

25:15|He gave one five talents, another two, and another one, each according to his ability. Then he left. At once,|Keeps the large monetary unit and the source position of immediately, continuing into the next verse.
25:16|the servant who received five talents went to work with them and gained five more.|Joins at-once to the servant’s action across the verse boundary.
25:17|In the same way, the servant with two gained two more.|Retains the parallel gain and relative amounts.
25:18|But the servant who received one went off, dug a hole, and hid his master’s money in the ground.|Makes the sequence concrete and keeps money rather than innate talent.
25:19|After a long time, the servants’ master returned and settled accounts with them.|Retains the lengthy delay and financial reckoning.

25:20|The servant who had received five talents came forward with five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted five talents to me. Look, I have gained five more.’|Clarifies speaker and action while retaining the repeated amounts.

25:21|His master said, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a little; I will put you in charge of much. Come and share your master’s joy.’|Makes entering joy idiomatic without replacing it with a specified reward.

25:22|The servant with two talents also came forward. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted two talents to me. Look, I have gained two more.’|Preserves the second report’s parallel form and distinct amount.

25:23|His master said, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a little; I will put you in charge of much. Come and share your master’s joy.’|Retains the identical response given for different sums.

25:24|Then the servant who had received one talent came forward. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘I knew you were a hard man. You reap where you have not sown and gather where you have not scattered seed.|Keeps the harsh assessment inside the servant’s speech and retains the agricultural images.
25:25|I was afraid, so I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here, you have what is yours.’|Preserves fear as the servant’s stated reason and the defensive return.

25:26|His master replied, ‘You wicked, lazy servant! You knew I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed?|Retains the question echoing the servant’s accusation without certifying the accusation as narrator fact.

25:27|Then you should have put my money with the bankers, so that when I returned I could have received it with interest.|Makes the counterfactual consequence clear while retaining bankers and interest.
25:28|So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.|Retains the transfer to the servant with ten, not an invented equal distribution.

25:29|For everyone who has will be given more and will have plenty. But whoever does not have will lose even what they have.|Preserves the paradox without supplying an unstated object such as faith or wealth.
25:30|Throw this useless servant into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.’|Retains the expulsion and repeated judgment image.
25:31|“When the Son of Man comes in his glory with all the angels, he will sit on his glorious throne.|Preserves the title, angels, and royal setting without additional identification.

25:32|All the nations will be gathered before him. He will separate people from one another as a shepherd separates sheep from goats.|Clarifies the shift from collective nations to people without restricting the participants.
25:33|He will place the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.|Retains the two-sided arrangement without adding symbolism.

25:34|Then the king will say to those on his right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by my Father. Inherit the kingdom prepared for you since the foundation of the world.|Preserves the shift to king and the prepared inheritance.

25:35|For I was hungry and you gave me food. I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink. I was a stranger and you welcomed me.|Makes each act audible while retaining the repeated first-person identification.
25:36|I was naked and you clothed me. I was sick and you cared for me. I was in prison and you came to me.’|Retains distinct clothing, care, and prison visitation actions.
25:37|Then the righteous will ask, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink?|Preserves the surprised question and first pair of actions.
25:38|When did we see you a stranger and welcome you, or naked and clothe you?|Retains the repeated question and second pair unchanged in sense.
25:39|When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’|Keeps coming to the person as the shared action.

25:40|The king will answer, ‘I tell you the truth: whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.’|Retains brothers and sisters of mine without deciding the disputed referent in the translation.

25:41|“Then he will say to those on his left, ‘Go away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.|Preserves the specified preparation for devil and angels without adding a claim about human predestination.
25:42|For I was hungry and you gave me no food. I was thirsty and you gave me nothing to drink.|Maintains the negative parallel to the earlier acts of care.

25:43|I was a stranger and you did not welcome me. I was naked and you did not clothe me. I was sick and in prison and you did not care for me.’|Retains all omitted actions and repeated first-person identification.

25:44|They too will ask, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty, a stranger or naked, sick or in prison, and fail to serve you?’|Makes the final negative verb idiomatic while preserving the complete list.

25:45|He will answer, ‘I tell you the truth: whatever you failed to do for one of the least of these, you failed to do for me.’|Retains the parallel with the positive answer and does not insert brothers absent here.
25:46|And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”|Uses the same adjective for punishment and life and marks the return to narrative conclusion.
26:1|When Jesus had finished saying all this, he told his disciples,|Connects the completed discourse to the prediction.
26:2|“You know that Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”|Retains the two-day timing and hand-over motif.
26:3|Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, Caiaphas.|Names the participants and location without adding scribes absent from this source.
26:4|They plotted to arrest Jesus by deception and kill him.|Preserves deceit and lethal intent.
26:5|“But not during the festival,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”|Makes the feared public reaction the reason for delay.
26:6|Jesus was in Bethany, at the house of Simon the leper.|Preserves Simon’s designation without inventing his medical history.

26:7|While he reclined at the table, a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume and poured it over his head.|Preserves the unnamed woman, head anointing, costly perfume, and reclining posture.
26:8|The disciples saw this and were indignant. “Why this waste?” they asked.|Keeps the objection with the disciples collectively rather than importing Judas alone.
26:9|“This could have been sold for a large sum and the money given to the poor.”|Supplies money as the natural object of the sale proceeds.
26:10|Aware of this, Jesus said, “Why are you troubling this woman? She has done something beautiful for me.|Renders the good deed idiom naturally without identifying the woman.
26:11|You always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.|Retains the temporal contrast rather than making it a prohibition on helping the poor.
26:12|By pouring this perfume on my body, she has prepared me for burial.|Makes the burial purpose readable without explaining the woman’s knowledge.

26:13|I tell you the truth: wherever this good news is proclaimed throughout the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”|Retains the worldwide proclamation and memorial to the woman.
26:14|Then one of the Twelve, Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests.|Preserves membership in the Twelve as part of the betrayal’s force.
26:15|“What will you give me if I hand him over to you?” he asked. They weighed out thirty silver coins for him.|Retains the hand-over network, weighing, number, and metal.
26:16|From then on, he looked for an opportunity to hand Jesus over.|Makes the referent clear while retaining repeated hand-over language.

26:17|On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal for you?”|Retains the festival timing and makes preparation’s object natural.

26:18|He said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My time is near. I will celebrate Passover at your house with my disciples.’”|Preserves the unnamed host and the Teacher’s first-person message.
26:19|The disciples did as Jesus directed and prepared the Passover meal.|Retains instruction followed by preparation.
26:20|When evening came, Jesus reclined at the table with the twelve disciples.|Keeps the meal posture and full group.
26:21|While they were eating, he said, “I tell you the truth: one of you will hand me over.”|Retains the meal setting and disturbing one-of-you announcement.
26:22|Deeply distressed, they began asking him one by one, “Surely not I, Lord?”|Preserves the question’s expectation of a negative reply.
26:23|He answered, “The one who dipped his hand in the bowl with me will hand me over.|Keeps the shared bowl and hand-over verb rather than expanding the identification.

26:24|The Son of Man goes as it is written about him. But woe to the man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been better for that man never to have been born.”|Preserves both scriptural necessity and the pronounced woe.
26:25|Judas, who was handing him over, asked, “Surely not I, Rabbi?” Jesus said to him, “You have said it.”|Retains Rabbi rather than harmonizing to Lord and leaves the indirect response intact.

26:26|As they ate, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing, and broke it. He gave it to the disciples and said, “Take, eat; this is my body.”|Makes successive actions audible without adding a sacramental explanation.
26:27|Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them. “Drink from it, all of you,” he said,|Preserves cup, thanksgiving, distribution, and the inclusive command.
26:28|“for this is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.|Retains Matthew’s forgiveness phrase and omits new absent from the pinned text.
26:29|I tell you, from now on I will not drink this fruit of the vine until the day I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.”|Preserves fruit-of-vine imagery and the promised shared drinking.
26:30|After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.|Retains the collective singing without naming an unstated psalm.

26:31|Then Jesus told them, “Tonight you will all fall away because of me, for it is written,\n‘I will strike the shepherd,\nand the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’|Retains all, the causal connection, and the scriptural poetry.
26:32|But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”|Preserves resurrection passive and the promised meeting location.
26:33|Peter answered, “Even if everyone falls away because of you, I never will.”|Retains Peter’s contrast between everyone and himself.
26:34|Jesus told him, “I tell you the truth: tonight, before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”|Preserves Matthew’s single rooster marker and three denials.
26:35|Peter said, “Even if I must die with you, I will never deny you!” All the disciples said the same.|Retains Peter’s emphatic refusal and the others’ shared confidence.

26:36|Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane. He told his disciples, “Sit here while I go over there to pray.”|Clarifies movement and instruction without adding a garden to Matthew’s place description.
26:37|He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him and began to feel sorrow and anguish.|Preserves the three companions and Jesus’ emotional distress.
26:38|He told them, “My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow, to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with me.”|Retains soul and death language alongside the request for shared watching.

26:39|Going a little farther, he fell facedown and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.”|Retains the cup metaphor, bodily posture, and contrast of wills.

26:40|He came back to the disciples and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “Could you not keep watch with me for even one hour?|Keeps the address to Peter with the plural challenge to the group documented in apparatus.
26:41|Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”|Retains the spirit/flesh contrast and temptation ambiguity in vocabulary.
26:42|He went away a second time and prayed, “My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will be done.”|Preserves the changed conditional formulation and the drinking image.
26:43|He returned and again found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.|Retains the bodily explanation for their sleep.
26:44|Leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words.|Preserves threefold prayer and repeated wording.

26:45|Then he came to the disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour has come. The Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.|Uses interrogative punctuation for the difficult opening, with the alternative retained in a note.
26:46|Get up; let us go. Look, the one handing me over is near.”|Retains the urgent commands and approaching betrayer without importing a name here.

26:47|While he was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived. With him was a large crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders of the people.|Preserves the timing, Judas’s membership, weapons, and commissioning authorities.
26:48|The man handing him over had given them a signal: “The one I kiss is the man. Arrest him.”|Retains the prearranged kiss and direct arrest command.
26:49|He immediately went up to Jesus. “Greetings, Rabbi!” he said, and kissed him.|Preserves the immediate approach, address, and enacted signal.

26:50|Jesus said to him, “Friend, do what you came for.” Then they stepped forward, seized Jesus, and arrested him.|Renders the elliptical address as a command while recording its uncertainty in a note.

26:51|One of those with Jesus reached for his sword, drew it, and struck the high priest’s slave, cutting off his ear.|Retains the unnamed swordsman and slave’s status; does not import another Gospel’s names.

26:52|Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back where it belongs. Everyone who takes up the sword will perish by the sword.|Preserves the repeated sword and warning without converting it into a modern policy statement.
26:53|Do you think I cannot appeal to my Father, and he would at once provide me with more than twelve legions of angels?|Keeps the military image and more-than-twelve number.
26:54|But how, then, would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say it must happen this way?”|Makes the scriptural necessity explicit in natural English syntax.

26:55|At that moment Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me as though I were a bandit? Day after day I sat teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me.|Preserves the armed arrest contrast and repeated public teaching.

26:56|But all this has happened so that the writings of the prophets may be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples abandoned him and fled.|Keeps fulfillment inside Jesus’ speech and the disciples’ flight as narrative.
26:57|Those who arrested Jesus led him to Caiaphas, the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.|Preserves the named destination and assembled participants.

26:58|Peter followed at a distance, as far as the high priest’s courtyard. He went inside and sat with the attendants to see how it would end.|Clarifies the route and Peter’s stated purpose without inventing motives.
26:59|The chief priests and the whole council were looking for false testimony against Jesus so they could put him to death.|Preserves the explicit falsity and intended execution.
26:60|Although many false witnesses came forward, they found none. At last two came forward|Retains the failed search and sentence continuing into the witnesses’ words.
26:61|and said, “This man said, ‘I can destroy God’s sanctuary and rebuild it in three days.’”|Distinguishes sanctuary from temple precinct and keeps the claim as reported testimony.
26:62|The high priest stood up and asked him, “Have you no answer? What is this testimony against you?”|Retains the two questions and pressure to respond.

26:63|But Jesus remained silent. The high priest said, “I put you under oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”|Preserves silence, solemn adjuration, and both titles.

26:64|Jesus answered, “You have said it. But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”|Retains indirect affirmation, Power as divine designation, and combined imagery.

26:65|Then the high priest tore his clothes. “He has blasphemed!” he said. “Why do we need any more witnesses? You have now heard the blasphemy.|Keeps the charge in the high priest’s speech rather than the narrator’s voice.
26:66|What is your judgment?” They answered, “He deserves death.”|Makes the council’s reply clear without treating it as the narrator’s verdict.
26:67|Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists. Others slapped him,|Preserves the distinct forms of physical abuse.
26:68|saying, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who hit you?”|Retains the title within the mocking demand.

26:69|Meanwhile Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant girl came up to him and said, “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”|Keeps the first accuser, location, and regional identification.
26:70|But he denied it in front of everyone. “I do not know what you are talking about,” he said.|Preserves the public denial and its indirect wording.

26:71|When he went out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and told the people there, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth.”|Retains the second woman and changed location without harmonization.
26:72|Again he denied it, this time with an oath: “I do not know the man.”|Preserves escalation from denial to sworn denial.
26:73|A little later the bystanders came up to Peter. “You certainly are one of them,” they said. “Your accent gives you away.”|Makes speech-based identification idiomatic.
26:74|Then he began to call down curses and swear, “I do not know the man!” Immediately a rooster crowed.|Retains curses without specifying their unstated target and keeps immediate crowing.
26:75|Peter remembered what Jesus had said: “Before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.|Preserves remembered prediction and the emotional conclusion.
27:1|Early in the morning, all the chief priests and elders of the people made plans to put Jesus to death.|Retains the collective deliberation and purpose.
27:2|They bound him, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate the governor.|Preserves the sequence and hand-over motif into Roman custody.

27:3|When Judas, who had handed him over, saw that Jesus was condemned, he was filled with remorse. He returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders.|Keeps remorse tied to the condemnation without resolving later theological judgments about repentance.

27:4|“I have sinned,” he said. “I have handed over innocent blood.” They replied, “What is that to us? That is your concern.”|Preserves innocent-blood idiom and the leaders’ rejection of responsibility.
27:5|He threw the silver coins into the sanctuary and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.|Retains the sanctuary location and manner of death without added detail.

27:6|The chief priests picked up the coins. “It is not lawful to put these into the treasury,” they said, “because they are blood money.”|Keeps the legal objection in their speech and the blood-money designation.
27:7|After discussing it, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.|Preserves the decision, purchase, and designated beneficiaries.
27:8|That is why the field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.|Retains the narrator’s naming explanation and temporal viewpoint.

27:9|Then what was spoken through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled:\n“They took the thirty silver coins,\nthe price set on him by some of the people of Israel,|Preserves the pinned attribution to Jeremiah and quoted price without silently correcting to Zechariah.
27:10|and gave them for the potter’s field,\nas the Lord directed me.”|Retains the quotation’s first-person close and divine instruction.
27:11|Jesus stood before the governor, who asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “You say so.”|Preserves the political title and indirect response.
27:12|When the chief priests and elders accused him, he gave no answer.|Retains silence in response to the specific accusers.
27:13|Then Pilate asked him, “Do you not hear how much they are testifying against you?”|Preserves Pilate’s appeal to the volume of testimony.
27:14|But Jesus did not answer him even a single word, to the governor’s great amazement.|Makes the emphatic silence and reaction audible.
27:15|At the festival, the governor customarily released one prisoner chosen by the crowd.|Retains the custom and the crowd’s role without adding a legal explanation.
27:16|At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas.|Preserves Jesus in Barabbas’s name as printed in the pinned text.
27:17|So when the crowd gathered, Pilate asked, “Whom do you want me to release for you: Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus who is called the Christ?”|Retains the deliberate contrast between the two names.
27:18|For he knew they had handed Jesus over out of envy.|Preserves the narrator’s explanation of Pilate’s knowledge.

27:19|While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him a message: “Have nothing to do with that righteous man. I have suffered greatly today in a dream because of him.”|Clarifies the messenger relationship and keeps righteous in the wife’s speech.
27:20|But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus killed.|Preserves the specific persuaders and two requested outcomes.
27:21|The governor asked them, “Which of the two do you want me to release for you?” “Barabbas,” they replied.|Retains the two-person choice and terse collective reply.
27:22|Pilate asked, “Then what should I do with Jesus who is called the Christ?” They all said, “Let him be crucified!”|Preserves the title and the crowd’s requested execution.
27:23|“Why?” he asked. “What evil has he done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Let him be crucified!”|Retains the unanswered question and escalating demand.

27:24|Pilate saw that he was getting nowhere and that a riot was beginning. He took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. “I am innocent of this blood,” he said. “That is your concern.”|Keeps Pilate’s claim as speech and preserves the repeated responsibility idiom.
27:25|All the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children!”|Retains the difficult words without expanding their speakers beyond this narrative scene.
27:26|Then he released Barabbas for them. After having Jesus flogged, he handed him over to be crucified.|Preserves Pilate’s agency in flogging and execution despite his preceding claim.

27:27|The governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the governor’s headquarters and gathered the whole cohort around him.|Identifies Roman actors and retains cohort as a military term explained in vocabulary.
27:28|They stripped him and put a scarlet cloak on him.|Preserves Matthew’s scarlet color without harmonizing to another Gospel.

27:29|They wove a crown of thorns, placed it on his head, and put a reed in his right hand. Kneeling before him, they mocked him: “Hail, king of the Jews!”|Preserves the mock royal props, bodily action, and address.
27:30|They spat on him, took the reed, and struck him on the head.|Keeps all three abusive actions without embellishment.
27:31|When they had finished mocking him, they removed the cloak, dressed him in his own clothes, and led him away to crucify him.|Preserves the transition from mockery to execution.
27:32|As they went out, they came upon a man from Cyrene named Simon and forced him to carry Jesus’ cross.|Retains origin, name, and coercion without inventing Simon’s motivation.
27:33|They came to a place called Golgotha, which means “Place of a Skull.”|Preserves the place name and the narrator’s explanation.
27:34|They offered Jesus wine mixed with gall. After tasting it, he refused to drink.|Retains gall rather than importing Mark’s myrrh.
27:35|After crucifying him, they divided his clothes by casting lots.|Preserves the casting of lots without inserting a source-absent fulfillment quotation.
27:36|Then they sat down and kept watch over him there.|Retains the soldiers’ watch at the execution site.
27:37|Above his head they placed the written charge against him: “This is Jesus, the king of the Jews.”|Preserves the complete inscription and its function as charge.
27:38|Two bandits were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.|Retains the two companions and their positions without characterizing their later responses differently.
27:39|Those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads|Keeps verbal and bodily mockery connected to the following speech.

27:40|and saying, “You who would destroy the sanctuary and rebuild it in three days, save yourself! If you are God’s Son, come down from the cross!”|Preserves the challenge’s conditional wording and its sanctuary accusation.
27:41|Likewise the chief priests, with the scribes and elders, mocked him, saying,|Keeps the specified group as the next speakers.

27:42|“He saved others; he cannot save himself! He is the king of Israel. Let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.|Retains save repeated and the taunting condition for belief.
27:43|He trusts in God. Let God rescue him now, if he wants him, for he said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”|Preserves the scriptural echo and the if-he-wants-him ambiguity.
27:44|The bandits crucified with him also insulted him in the same way.|Retains Matthew’s plural without importing another Gospel’s repentant individual.
27:45|From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land.|Renders the sixth-to-ninth hours naturally while leaving land/earth range in a note.

27:46|About three in the afternoon, Jesus cried out loudly, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” That means, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”|Retains Matthew’s transliteration and quoted lament without explaining away abandonment.
27:47|Some of those standing there heard him and said, “This man is calling Elijah.”|Preserves the hearers’ misunderstanding as their speech.

27:48|Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and offered him a drink.|Retains the urgent sequence and distinguishes sour wine from earlier gall mixture.
27:49|The others said, “Leave him alone. Let us see whether Elijah comes to save him.”|Keeps the waiting taunt without adding the spear variant absent from the pinned text.
27:50|Jesus cried out loudly once more and gave up his spirit.|Retains repeated cry and spirit idiom rather than adding an explanation of his death.
27:51|Then the sanctuary curtain was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split.|Preserves direction, sanctuary curtain, and accompanying upheaval.
27:52|The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy people who had fallen asleep were raised.|Retains bodies, holy people, sleep metaphor, and passive raising.

27:53|After Jesus’ resurrection, they came out of the tombs, entered the holy city, and appeared to many.|Names Jesus to clarify whose resurrection sets the timing, without inventing subsequent events.

27:54|When the centurion and those guarding Jesus with him saw the earthquake and what had happened, they were terrified. “This man truly was God’s Son!” they said.|Preserves the shared confession and military witnesses.
27:55|Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee and cared for him.|Retains the women’s continued presence and prior service.
27:56|Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.|Preserves all three identifications without supplying the third woman’s name.
27:57|When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived. He too had become a disciple of Jesus.|Retains wealth, origin, and discipleship without importing council membership.
27:58|He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Pilate ordered it to be given to him.|Preserves the request and the governor’s authorization.
27:59|Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.|Keeps the specified material and cleanness.
27:60|He laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut into the rock. Then he rolled a large stone across the entrance and left.|Retains ownership, newness, rock cutting, and closure.
27:61|Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.|Preserves the two witnesses and their position.
27:62|The next day, the day after Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate.|Retains Matthew’s calendar phrasing and the changed group of authorities.

27:63|“Sir,” they said, “we remember that while that deceiver was still alive, he said, ‘After three days I will be raised.’|Keeps deceiver inside their accusation and preserves the quoted prediction.

27:64|So order the tomb to be secured until the third day. Otherwise his disciples may come and steal him, then tell the people, ‘He has been raised from the dead.’ This last deception would be worse than the first.”|Retains their feared scenario as a claim, not narrator fact.
27:65|Pilate told them, “You have a guard. Go and secure it as best you know how.”|Preserves the ambiguous have-a-guard wording; imperative alternative goes in a note.
27:66|They went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone and posting the guard.|Makes the securing actions readable without elaborating the seal’s physical form.

28:1|After the Sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.|Preserves Matthew’s two named visitors and stated purpose without importing spices.

28:2|Suddenly there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, came to the tomb, rolled away the stone, and sat on it.|Retains the causal connection and the angel’s actions without claiming the stone released Jesus.
28:3|His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow.|Preserves both similes without specifying human ethnicity.
28:4|The guards shook with fear of him and became like dead men.|Retains the fear response and death comparison.
28:5|The angel said to the women, “Do not be afraid. I know you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified.|Keeps reassurance addressed to the women and identifies the crucified Jesus.
28:6|He is not here; he has been raised, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay.|Preserves passive raised and the invitation to inspect the empty place.

28:7|Then go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has been raised from the dead and is going ahead of you into Galilee. You will see him there.’ Remember, I have told you.”|Retains the commission, place, promised sight, and angel’s closing reminder.
28:8|They quickly left the tomb, afraid yet filled with great joy, and ran to tell his disciples.|Preserves simultaneous fear and joy and the women’s urgent action.
28:9|Suddenly Jesus met them. “Greetings!” he said. They came to him, took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.|Retains the physical encounter, greeting, and worship action.

28:10|Then Jesus told them, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to leave for Galilee. They will see me there.”|Retains brothers for the disciple-directed message without expanding its referent here.

28:11|While the women were on their way, some of the guard went into the city and reported everything that had happened to the chief priests.|Clarifies the concurrent movements and keeps some rather than all guards.
28:12|The chief priests met with the elders and devised a plan. They gave the soldiers a large sum of money|Preserves the planning and payment before the quoted instruction.
28:13|and told them, “Say, ‘His disciples came at night and stole him while we were asleep.’|Keeps the theft account explicitly within the instructed false report.
28:14|If the governor hears about this, we will persuade him and keep you out of trouble.”|Renders freedom-from-anxiety idiom naturally in the threatened official consequences.

28:15|The soldiers took the money and did as they were instructed. This story has circulated among the Jews to this day.|Preserves the narrator’s report without implying agreement by every Jewish person.
28:16|The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had appointed for them.|Retains eleven, location, and prior direction without naming the mountain.
28:17|When they saw him, they worshiped him, but some hesitated.|Renders distazō as hesitation while retaining the tension alongside worship.
28:18|Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.|Preserves the comprehensive authority and passive gift.

28:19|So go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,|Keeps disciple-making central, all nations, singular name, and the threefold baptismal expression.
